description: The PR-metadata half of the readability policy. The code change is small and well documented (the MAX_JOBS_PER_PASS comment carries the why and is a must-not-flag trap), but the PR description is built entirely from metaphors ('teaches the drain loop to breathe', 'shoulders a bite-sized batch', 'land cleanly before the health check wakes up') and never states the cap or the deadline in plain terms. The reviewer must return ONE finding with no path/line (the PR-level form that folds into the review body), quoting the description and giving the plain rewrite in the prose.

evidence_trace: pr-context.json description: "This change teaches the drain loop to breathe. Each pass now shoulders a bite-sized batch and has to land cleanly before the health check wakes up and starts asking questions; anything left over waits patiently for the next breath."
the diff caps a drain pass at MAX_JOBS_PER_PASS = 50 against the worker's 60s health-check interval; the description names neither number and no concrete operation
finding.failure_scenario: A reviewer or a future archaeologist reading the PR list cannot tell from the description what the change does (cap each drain pass at 50 jobs so a pass finishes inside the 60s health-check window) without opening the diff.
finding.model_authored_prose: The description requires translating its metaphors to recover the change: "teaches the drain loop to breathe", "shoulders a bite-sized batch", "has to land cleanly before the health check wakes up". Plainer: "Cap each drain pass at MAX_JOBS_PER_PASS (50) so a pass finishes inside the worker's 60s health-check interval instead of being killed mid-drain; remaining jobs are picked up by the next pass."
